motion.purpose: Region selection travel; immediate under reduced motion

reading.ground: sea, no card background or shadow
reading.scroll: independent desktop and landscape; document portrait

experienceFidelity.behavior: Visitors can drag the diorama horizontally, swipe with trusted touch, turn through keyboard arrows or use West/East buttons. The bounded orbit changes how the islands overlap and reveals shore depth. Island geometry is raycast-selectable; existing region approaches, atlas margins, next-shore and contact reading remain. Phone shore controls moved into open water after the inspection found title overlap. Offscreen atlas stops rendering.
experienceFidelity.limits: The source original stayed on LOADING during live revisit; drag instructions and retained archived imagery informed this interpretation, not a claimed successful live gesture test. No source-level populated character performance, day/night system or horizontal narrative world. Camera travel is frame-based and slows substantially in software rendering (4 desktop / 13 phone renders per second observed). A 2.5-second pause snapshot had four remaining approach frames; longer diagnostic reached zero. A 390px offscreen probe left a 15px scenic strip visible and therefore continued rendering; a truly offscreen 320px probe showed zero delta. Hidden-tab behavior could not be certified because the headless browser kept document.hidden false.

components.name: Whole archipelago

narrative.overview: The accepted archipelago remains unchanged. Distinct atlas-margin reading uses the sea ground, coral annotation rules and peach Gloock lead, with a map-first portrait composition and accessible next-shore navigation.

rules.name: No scene dependency
rules.body: Every story is available through native controls even if WebGL fails.
